decisions.reason: Apron connectivity builds on the firm's integration and installed-equipment knowledge and enables its data platform, so in-house R&D can keep learning from deployments and improving it.

Billing software sits furthest from the firm's engineering knowledge base, which limits how well it can learn from results, but it still rounds out the integrated suite and is cheap to keep for another year.
Equipment monitoring draws directly on the firm's maintenance and field expertise, so it can interpret field data well and use it to strengthen the growing service business.

Apron resource management is close to the core offer, but with turnaround management (Product A) withdrawn, its overlap with neighbouring modules warrants watching, though it still fits the automation strategy.
The controller safety alert service extends the firm's tower and surveillance know-how, where its own R&D can absorb controller feedback and improve the service.
